title: What should a weekly meal-prep quote include?
body_html:
A weekly meal-prep quote should specify who you are feeding, how many portions you will receive, when cooking happens, and what the chef will do before leaving. It should also separate groceries, shopping, containers, dietary requests and kitchen cleanup from the cooking itself. Compare the written scope, not just the headline total.

Start with private chef services in Dubai and the current weekly meal-prep plans. Compare the written inclusions against your brief rather than treating this guide as a separate rate card.

TL;DR
  • Weekly meal prep quote inclusions should define portions, cooking visits, groceries, storage and cleanup.
  • myCHEF provides vetted chefs for household cooking and weekly meal preparation.
  • Ask for written exclusions and change terms before agreeing to recurring cooking.
  • Compare proposals against the same household brief, not different definitions of a meal.

What should a weekly meal-prep quote include?

A useful quote describes the food you will receive and the work needed to prepare it. You should be able to understand the arrangement without filling gaps yourself.

If you are still deciding what kind of support you need, the guide to meal-prep services in Dubai provides a starting point for comparing service formats. Once you request proposals, give each provider the same brief.

Use this checklist to assess the scope:

Quote item What the written proposal should clarify What to question
Household coverage People, meals and individual portions Whether a dish serves one person or the household
Cooking schedule Visit frequency, agreed dates and session scope Whether shopping and cleanup sit inside the session
Menu planning Dishes, preferences and approval process Whether revisions or extra dishes change the scope
Groceries Who buys, who pays and how substitutions work Whether ingredients are included or separate
Dietary requirements Restrictions and the provider's agreed approach Whether a request has actually been accepted
Containers and storage Who supplies containers and how food is labelled Whether suitable storage space is required
Kitchen handover Equipment used and cleanup responsibilities Which surfaces, utensils and appliances are covered
Changes and exclusions Rescheduling, cancellations and additional work What happens when your household plans change

A clear quote makes responsibilities visible on both sides. That protects your routine as well as your budget.

Why does the scope matter more than the headline total?

Two proposals are not comparable if one covers cooking alone and the other also covers shopping, portioning and kitchen handover. The difference is work, not wording.

Before deciding, mark each item as included, separately charged, supplied by you or not offered. An unanswered item is a question to resolve, not an inclusion to assume.

myCHEF weekly meal prep is for households that want a vetted chef to cook at home. The practical trade-off is that home cooking needs access to your kitchen, suitable equipment and storage; it does not remove every household responsibility.

Keep recurring household meals separate from entertaining. A birthday dinner or a single hosted evening needs an event brief, even when the number of diners matches your usual household.

How should the quote define meals and portions?

Ask for individual portions rather than relying on the word meals. A family-style dish and a separately packed lunch describe different outcomes, even when both appear as one menu item.

For an illustrative brief, 2 adults needing lunch on 5 working days require 10 individual lunch portions. That is a planning example, not a myCHEF package or a recommendation about how long food should be stored.

Your quote should distinguish:

  • People: who will eat the food, including children where relevant.
  • Eating occasions: lunches, dinners or another agreed requirement.
  • Portions: how much prepared food each person needs.
  • Menu variety: repeated dishes versus different recipes.
  • Packing: shared containers or individual servings.

Explain appetite differences and whether sides belong in the portion count. If you expect a main dish, vegetables and a separate salad, write that down rather than assuming the word dinner covers everything.

Do not treat a portion count as a storage plan. Ask how preparation, refrigeration, freezing and reheating will work for the particular dishes agreed.

What should menu planning and dietary requests cover?

The quote should explain who proposes the menu, when you approve it and what happens if you ask for changes. A list of favourite cuisines helps, but concrete preferences are more useful: preferred ingredients, disliked textures, spice levels and dishes that reheat well for your routine.

Distinguish preferences from restrictions. Avoiding an ingredient because you dislike it is not the same brief as managing an allergy or a medically prescribed diet.

Ask the provider to confirm:

  • Which dietary requirements they have accepted.
  • How ingredient labels and substitutions will be checked.
  • Whether separate preparation or equipment is required.
  • Which requests fall outside the agreed service.

For halal requirements, state what you expect for ingredients and sourcing rather than relying on a broad cuisine description. For allergies, do not interpret a willingness to discuss the menu as a guarantee about cross-contact.

If you need nutrition calculations, request their scope explicitly. A tailored menu does not automatically include measured portions, calculated macros or medical dietary advice.

Are groceries and shopping included in a weekly meal-prep quote?

Groceries and shopping need separate answers. A chef can plan ingredients without purchasing them, and a shopping arrangement does not by itself tell you how ingredients are paid for.

Ask who prepares the shopping list, who places orders and who receives deliveries. Then confirm whether you approve purchases beforehand and how receipts or reimbursements are handled.

Ingredient substitutions deserve their own agreement. Specify whether the chef should contact you before replacing an unavailable ingredient, particularly where allergies, religious requirements or strong preferences apply.

Also clarify pantry use. Salt, oil and spices already in your kitchen should not become an assumed supply without discussion. Ask whether the chef checks them before the visit and whether replenishment is your responsibility.

Do not read grocery management as automatic restocking. If you want someone to monitor supplies between visits, ask whether that work is offered and included.

What should cooking visits and kitchen access include?

A recurring arrangement needs a practical arrival and departure plan. Confirm the visit schedule, where cooking takes place and how the chef will enter the property.

For a Dubai apartment or villa, include building access instructions, parking arrangements and any reception or security process that affects arrival. Describe these as your property's arrangements, not requirements that apply everywhere.

Share an accurate equipment list before the quote is finalised. Mention the hob, oven, fridge, freezer, useful small appliances and any equipment that does not work reliably.

Use this sequence to prepare the brief:

  1. Household brief: describe who needs meals and when they eat.
  2. Kitchen check: share equipment, access and storage details.
  3. Scope approval: agree the menu, tasks and exclusions.
  4. Visit handover: confirm what will be packed, labelled and cleaned.

If another household member will receive the chef, give that person the agreed brief. Avoid having access instructions, menu changes and dietary information split across several conversations.

Should containers, labels and cleanup be included?

The quote should state who supplies containers and whether the chef will portion the food into them. Do not assume that cooking includes purchasing packaging or reorganising your fridge.

Agree what labels should communicate. Dish names, preparation details and dish-specific storage or reheating instructions help the person eating later understand the handover. Ask the provider to explain the guidance rather than applying one storage rule to every recipe.

Cleanup needs equally concrete wording. Ask whether it covers the utensils used, work surfaces, hob and sink, and where washed equipment will be left.

Clarify the kitchen's starting condition too. Cleaning up after cooking is different from clearing an existing pile of dishes or completing a wider household clean.

The strongest handover description tells you what you will find when the chef leaves. Prepared food, usable storage and an agreed kitchen reset are clearer than an undefined promise to take care of everything.

Why do weekly meal-prep quotes vary?

The work changes when the household brief changes. Use these factors to explain differences between proposals, then ask each provider to identify which ones affect its quote:

  • Portion volume: the number of people and eating occasions to cover.
  • Menu complexity: distinct recipes, preparation methods and separate components.
  • Dietary adaptations: ingredient checks, substitutions and separate preparation requests.
  • Shopping responsibility: list preparation, purchasing and delivery coordination.
  • Visit arrangements: cooking frequency, access and the equipment available.
  • Handover scope: individual packing, labelling and cleanup tasks.

A shorter menu with repeated dishes simplifies the brief, but repetition is only useful if your household will eat the results. More variety gives you different meals; it also creates more dishes and ingredients to coordinate.

Choose the balance around your routine. Ask the provider to explain the effect of each change rather than assuming a smaller menu automatically produces a particular saving.

How do you compare proposals fairly?

Send the same written brief to each provider. Ask for answers against the checklist above so you can distinguish a different service scope from a different total.

An illustrative comparison shows why this matters: a proposal for 10 portions across several dishes is not equivalent to a proposal for 10 dishes with no serving quantities. Neither wording establishes how many lunches your household will receive unless the portions are defined.

Before accepting, check three things:

  • Output: you understand the dishes, portions and packing.
  • Responsibility: you know who handles ingredients, equipment and storage.
  • Changes: you understand rescheduling, cancellations and extra requests.

Request a revised written scope when a conversation changes the arrangement. A helpful verbal answer should become part of the proposal you approve.

FAQ

What are the essential weekly meal prep quote inclusions?

Weekly meal prep quote inclusions should cover portions, menus, cooking visits, groceries, dietary requests, containers, storage handover and cleanup. The proposal should also identify exclusions and change terms.

Does a weekly meal-prep quote include ingredients?

Ingredients are included only when the proposal explicitly says so. Confirm who shops, who pays, how purchases are approved and how substitutions are handled.

How do I tell a chef how many meals I need?

Describe individual portions and eating occasions rather than using meals alone. For example, 2 adults needing lunch on 5 working days require 10 individual lunch portions; this is an illustrative brief, not a service package.

Can I ask for different meals for different family members?

Yes, include each person's requirements in the initial brief and ask the provider to confirm what it can accommodate. Separate dishes and dietary adaptations need an agreed scope.

Will the chef bring containers and cooking equipment?

Containers and cooking equipment should not be assumed to be included. Confirm what the chef brings and what must be ready in your kitchen.

Does weekly meal prep include washing up?

Washing up is included only to the extent described in the agreed scope. Ask specifically about used utensils, surfaces, the hob and the sink.

What happens if I need to change a cooking visit?

Changes depend on the booking terms you agree with the provider. Request the rescheduling, cancellation and additional-work terms before starting recurring visits.

Related guides

  • Meal prep for busy executives in Dubai
  • From a monthly chef booking to a weekly meal plan

Before you request your quote

Add one easily missed detail to your brief: who will reheat and serve the food. Meals eaten at an office need a different packing discussion from shared dinners served at home.

For a tailored myCHEF weekly meal-prep enquiry, share your preferred start date, Dubai location, household or guest count, and the service required. Include the meals you want covered, dietary requirements and kitchen arrangements so the proposed scope reflects your actual week.
